description:
This figure is a line graph comparing the training cost of three optimization algorithms over 45 iterations. The series are labeled as AdaGrad, SGDNesterov, and Adam. AdaGrad starts highest at 0.7 and decreases steadily, ending at around 0.45. SGDNesterov starts lower at 0.3 and also decreases, ending at around 0.25. Adam starts at 0.7 and decreases rapidly, ending at around 0.25. The graph shows the training cost decreasing for all algorithms over time.

Legend: AdaGrad, SGDNesterov, Adam
Axis: Iterations, Training cost
Series: AdaGrad (highest), SGDNesterov (lowest), Adam (middle)

caption: Figure 1: Logistic regression training negative log likelihood on MNIST images and IMDB movie reviews with 10,000 bag-of-words (BoW) feature vectors.
description:
This figure is a line graph comparing the training negative log likelihood of logistic regression on two datasets: MNIST images and IMDB movie reviews with 10,000 bag-of-words (BoW) feature vectors. Four optimization algorithms are compared: Adagrad+dropout, RMSProp+dropout, SGDNesterov+dropout, and Adam+dropout. The red line (SGDNesterov+dropout) starts highest and decreases steadily, ending lowest. The blue line (Adagrad+dropout) starts lower and also decreases, ending higher than the red line but lower than the others. The green line (RMSProp+dropout) and the cyan line (Adam+dropout) start at similar levels and decrease, with the green line ending slightly higher than the cyan line.

Text in figure: "IMDb BoW feature Logistic Regression", "Adagrad+dropout", "RMSProp+dropout", "SGDNesterov+dropout", "Adam+dropout", "training cost", "iterations over entire dataset".

caption: Figure 2: Training of multilayer neural networks on MNIST images. (a) Neural networks using dropout stochastic regularization. (b) Neural networks with deterministic cost function. We compare with the sum-of-functions (SFO) optimizer (Sohl-Dickstein et al., 2014)
description:
Description: The figure contains two plots comparing various optimization algorithms on MNIST datasets. Plot (a) shows training costs over iterations for algorithms with dropout regularization. The AdaGrad line is highest, followed by RMSProp, SGDNesterov, AdaDelta, and Adam, which is the lowest. Plot (b) compares SFO and Adam optimizers, with Adam showing lower training costs.

Text in figure: MNIST Multilayer Neural Network + dropout, AdaGrad, RMSProp, SGDNesterov, AdaDelta, Adam, MNIST Multilayer Neural Networks, SFO, Adam, training cost, iterations over entire dataset, normalized walltime.

caption: Figure 3: Convolutional neural networks training cost. (left) Training cost for the first three epochs. (right) Training cost over 45 epochs. CIFAR-10 with c64-c64-c128-1000 architecture.
description:
Figure: Two line graphs showing training cost over iterations for convolutional neural networks on the CIFAR-10 dataset. Left graph: First three epochs. Right graph: 45 epochs. Series: AdaGrad, AdaGrad+dropout, SGD Nesterov, SGD Nesterov+dropout, Adam, Adam+dropout. Highest: AdaGrad (left), SGD Nesterov (right). Lowest: Adam+dropout (both graphs).

caption: Figure 4: Effect of bias-correction terms (red line) versus no bias correction terms (green line) after 10 epochs (left) and 100 epochs (right) on the loss (y-axes) when learning a Variational AutoEncoder (VAE) (Kingma & Welling, 2013), for different settings of stepsize α (x-axes) and hyperparameters β 1 and β 2 .
description:
This figure contains two panels, each with six subplots, showing the effect of bias-correction terms on the loss of a Variational AutoEncoder (VAE) after 10 and 100 epochs. Each subplot compares the loss with bias correction (red line) to the loss without bias correction (green line) for different values of stepsize α and hyperparameters β1 and β2. The highest loss is observed in the subplot with β2=0.9999 and β1=0.9, with the red line peaking at approximately 140. The lowest loss is seen in the subplot with β2=0.9999 and β1=0, with the green line dipping to around 100.
